title: NSIC Rc 31SR (Malagkit 6) Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: NSIC Rc 31SR is a glutinous inbred rice for irrigated lowland: about 124 days and 4.7 tonnes per hectare on average. See its pest ratings and grain quality.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 31SR is a glutinous inbred rice variety for irrigated lowland, known locally as Malagkit 6. The NSIC approved it in 2017. It matures in about 124 days and averages 4.7 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 10.8 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for rice variety 31SR, or Rc 31SR, this is the one. Compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 31SR yield?

On average it gives 4.7 tonnes per hectare. That is about 94 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits below the average of the 118 irrigated lowland inbreds on the list, which is 5.2 tonnes. But the top yield, 10.8 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 124 days from sowing to harvest. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as medium duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [bacterial leaf blight](/diseases/bacterial-leaf-blight), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.
Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant together with the farms around you, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 31SR?
items.a: It is known as Malagkit 6. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 31SR take to harvest?
items.a: About 124 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 31SR?
items.a: It averages 4.7 tonnes per hectare, about 94 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 10.8 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In trials it was weak against bacterial leaf blight, tungro, sheath blight. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
